subject.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access

question: How should upgrades handle existing trigger-script jobs whose persisted payload has no toolsAllow cap and whose original creator tool scope cannot be reconstructed?
rationale: The patch can safely cap new and edited jobs, but source data cannot distinguish or reconstruct the correct authorization policy for every legacy job; choosing compatibility, fail-closed behavior, or an explicit audit flow is a product-security decision.

options.title: Preserve and surface an audit
options.body: Keep legacy jobs running, but add a visible startup or doctor warning plus an operator workflow to approve or restamp uncapped trigger jobs.

options.title: Fail closed on legacy jobs
options.body: Disable or reject uncapped trigger scripts after upgrade until an operator explicitly assigns or approves a tool cap.

options.title: Accept new-and-edited protection
options.body: Merge the current behavior and document that existing uncapped jobs remain unchanged until their next trusted edit.

recommendation.title: Preserve and surface an audit
recommendation.body: Keep legacy jobs running, but add a visible startup or doctor warning plus an operator workflow to approve or restamp uncapped trigger jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the central cron service, gateway, persistence, and security-sensitive runtime surfaces affected by the upgrade choice.
